article_title: Celebrating 30 Years of K-12 Educational Programing at Fermilab
citation: M. Bardeen, M. P. Cooke. (2011). Celebrating 30 Years of K-12 Educational Programming at Fermilab. Proceedings of the DPF-2011 Conference, Providence, RI. http://ed.fnal.gov
title: I2U2 and QuarkNet e-Labs: student-led, teacher-guided online research projects built around students' own questions
description: The e-Labs are online projects in which high school students organize and conduct authentic research using real detector data and grid computing tools through a web browser. The authors state that "From start to finish e-Labs are student-led, teacher-guided projects" and that a project map with milestones lets students set the research plan rather than follow a step-by-step process. CMS, Cosmic Ray and LIGO e-Labs explore using the Internet and distributed computing in high school classes.
requirements: Students need only a web browser to access the grid techniques employed by professional researchers
target_learning_goals: experiencing the environment of scientific collaborations
examples: The CMS e-Lab uses a project map with milestones so students set the research plan; online data come from DZero, CDF, CMS and student cosmic ray detectors.
key_sources: M. Bardeen, M. P. Cooke. (2011). Celebrating 30 Years of K-12 Educational Programming at Fermilab. Proceedings of the DPF-2011 Conference, Providence, RI. https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.4630
